title.narrative: ROAP/LA/S1-32QXB-000728 - Lao PDR COVID-19 Response Project - Assessing of Health Facility and Lifeline Infrastructure for Health Emergency Preparedness in Lao PDR

description.narrative:
This project is a technical contribution to the broader technical assistance project entitled “Strengthening Health Facility and Lifeline Infrastructure for Health Emergency Preparedness in Lao PDR.“ The broader project is part of the Lao PDR COVID-19 Response Project which has received financial support of US$ 33 million through the World Bank’s IDA loan and HERP-Trust Fund aimed at responding to the COVID-19 pandemic and enhancing the preparedness and resilience of healthcare facilities and workers. The project has two components: 1. A national assessment to understand the spatial extent of multi-hazard risk under the current and future climate in Lao PDR and how they affect health facilities and critical infrastructure such as electricity, water, and transport networks in Lao PDR’s 17 provinces. 2. The development and piloting of a national hospital safety assessment based on the WHO Hospital Safety Index. UN-Habitat will build on the methodology previously used in a national climate vulnerability assessment, which included information on hospitals and health centres. Data will be collected through partnership with Ministry of Health offices at subnational levels. The proposed methodology will allow the quantification of risk to key public health facilities and related critical infrastructure from natural disasters and climate change-induced events such as floods, earthquakes, wildfires, landslides and drought across all Lao PDR provinces by analyzing the exposure to each hazard of all the health facilities across the country. The exposure data will be combined with vulnerability data obtained from questionnaires, and on-site assessments of health facilities to give a complete profile of each facility’s risk from multiple hazards. UN Habitat will design an appropriate set of questions that will complement the existing data on health facilities and related critical infrastructure across the country by identifying and filling the existing gaps. At the same time the questionnaire will enable a multi-hazard exposure analysis of the health facilities and critical infrastructure, quantifying the risks, their interdependencies, and the cascading consequences of health services disruption
*Notes: After the PRC in January 2023, the donor extended its scope and added 2 outputs. Because of this, the project budget increased. (See revised ProDoc with track changes.) The agreement with the revised duration and budget has been signed in May 2023.
